newsitem.title: USA: AFL-CIO leader says UPS strike highlights greed.
newsitem.headline: AFL-CIO leader says UPS strike highlights greed.

text.p: The strike against United Parcel Service highlights "corporate greed" in the United States and will benefit the union movement, AFL-CIO President John Sweeney said Friday.

"This strike is really putting the spotlight on corporate greed in this country and on the conditions workers are faced with and the trend towards part-time workers," Sweeney told delegates at the Texas convention of the labour group.

He said the AFL-CIO would give financial help to UPS strikers so they can keep the strike going to get a satisfactory settlement. The strike began on Monday after talks broke off over pay, the use of part-time workers, pensions and other issues.
After Sweeney's speech, five busloads of convention delegates travelled to Austin's UPS headquarters to walk picket lines in a show of solidarity with striking Teamsters.

Sweeney said he did not think the strike would cause a backlash against unions, but instead "could mobilise the labour movement and workers in other regions and industries in support of these strikers.
"It's an indication of how strong unions have to be to achieve some improvement," Sweeney said of the strike.
Sweeney's visit to the convention was part of a multi-city tour by AFL-CIO leadership aimed at boosting union membership, which now encompasses only about 11 percent of the U.S. work force.
"Just stabilising our membership will cost $300 million a year," Sweeney told the convention. "So we're asking all our labour bodies to shift resource and staff into organising on a massive scale."

Texas union leaders said one focus of their efforts will the state's growing high-technology sector. Sweeney said the AFL-CIO will be "organizing high-wage, as well as low-wage, high-tech, every industry, every part of the country."
